title: Federal Judge Temporarily Blocks Trump's $1.8B Anti-Weaponization Fund After Jan. 6 Prosecutor Lawsuit
detail: US District Judge Leonie Brinkema (E.D. Virginia) temporarily blocked Trump's $1.8 billion 'Anti-Weaponization Fund' on May 29, 2026 after a Jan. 6 prosecutor and Capitol Police officers filed suit challenging the fund's legality. The fund — created by executive order — was intended to compensate Trump allies and Jan. 6 defendants who claimed they were targeted by politically-motivated prosecutions. Judge Brinkema set a hearing for June 12. Critics argue the fund is unconstitutional as a violation of the separation of powers — only Congress can appropriate funds and settle lawsuits. The blocking order comes as Senate Republicans also face growing pressure from colleagues who want to rein in the unprecedented payout mechanism.

media.caption: Federal judge temporarily blocks Trump's $1.8 billion Anti-Weaponization Fund after Jan. 6 prosecutor and Capitol Police officers file suit

title: Trump Signs Executive Order Rescinding Off-Road Vehicle Restrictions on Federal Lands
detail: President Trump signed an executive order on May 29, 2026 rescinding two decades-old restrictions on off-road vehicle (ORV) access to federal public lands — specifically revoking Executive Orders 11644 (Nixon, 1972) and 11989 (Carter, 1977), which had required agencies to close off-road vehicle trails that caused environmental damage. The new order restores expanded recreational access to hundreds of millions of acres of federal land, allowing ORV users, hunters, and energy developers greater access. Environmental groups immediately pledged legal challenges, arguing the order opens sensitive ecosystems to vehicle damage and removes critical protections for endangered species habitats. The action aligns with Trump's broader 'energy dominance' and public lands access agenda.

media.caption: Trump signs EO rescinding Nixon- and Carter-era restrictions on off-road vehicle access to federal public lands

title: US and Iran Reach Tentative 60-Day Ceasefire Extension; Strait of Hormuz Reopening Framework Drafted
detail: The United States and Iran reached a tentative agreement on May 29, 2026 to extend the fragile ceasefire for 60 days, begin formal nuclear dismantlement talks, and reopen the Strait of Hormuz to international shipping. Under the draft framework, Iran would be required to remove all remaining naval mines from the Strait within 30 days and could not impose transit tolls. Defense Secretary Hegseth stated Iran was 'coming in our direction' and that talks were 'productive.' US military commanders warned they remained 'ready to resume combat' in the Gulf if Iran violated terms. Trump simultaneously announced via Truth Social the naval blockade would be 'lifted' for ships already caught in the Strait. The tentative deal followed days of maximum-strain ceasefire violations, including Kuwait's interception of an Iranian ballistic missile on May 28.

media.caption: US and Iran reach tentative 60-day ceasefire extension; Strait of Hormuz reopening framework drafted
